newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher as yen weakens.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher as yen weakens.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures extended early gains to ended higher across the board on Friday, as the yen weakened further against the dollar in the afternoon session, traders said.
Prices ranged from 20 yen to 100 yen per tonne higher.
Benchmark July 1998 closed 90 yen higher at 13,200 yen per tonne. Estimated volume was 24,664 lots.

"Activity was lacklustre earlier in the day as the fall overnight in Chicago was offset by the stronger dollar, but the yen's further weakening stimulated sporadic short-covering late in the day," one trader said.
Focus is on USDA report to be released later today.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.47-1/2 per bushel at 0806 GMT, against $2.47-3/4 at Thursday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean contract was traded at $7.80-1/2 per bushel at 0807 GMT, against $7.79 at Thursday's close.
